title: Atomic Structure
subject: Chemistry
description: Protons, neutrons, electrons, isotopes, ions and electron shells.
author: StudyDeck sample

cards.back: Positive particle in the nucleus. Relative mass 1, relative charge +1.
Neutral particle in the nucleus. Relative mass 1, relative charge 0.
Negative particle in shells around the nucleus. Very small mass, relative charge −1.
The number of protons in an atom.
cards.hint: It is the smaller number shown on the periodic table.

cards.back: The total number of protons and neutrons in an atom.
Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
An atom or group of atoms with an electric charge, formed by losing or gaining electrons.

cards.front: What a group number tells you
cards.back: The number of electrons in the outer shell (for groups 1 to 7).

cards.front: What a period number tells you
cards.back: The number of occupied electron shells.
Group 0 elements. They have a full outer shell, so they are very unreactive.

questions.question: Carbon-14 has an atomic number of 6. How many neutrons does it have?
Which particle has the smallest mass?
options: They all have the same mass
questions.explanation: An electron's mass is about 1/1836 of a proton's, so it is usually treated as negligible.

questions.question: Chlorine has 17 electrons. What is its electronic configuration?
questions.explanation: Fill the shells in order: 2 in the first, 8 in the second, and the remaining 7 in the third.

questions.question: Why are the noble gases so unreactive?
options: They have a full outer shell of electrons
They are gases at room temperature
questions.explanation: A full outer shell is stable, so noble gases do not need to gain, lose or share electrons.

questions.question: A magnesium atom loses 2 electrons. What does it become?
questions.explanation: Losing two negative electrons leaves two more protons than electrons, so it forms Mg²⁺.
